category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough.title='When the child confuses PERIMETER with AREA — repairing the around-vs-inside trap at Grade 3' references area but never explicitly bridges to Lesson 2 (Compare Areas) which begins immediately after; no 'tomorrow Roo will...' or back-reference forward in lesson_01.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add a one-line forward bridge near the end of consolidation or in expanded_walkthrough that explicitly tees up Lesson 2: e.g., 'Roo says: TOMORROW we measure AREA — the SPACE INSIDE. Today the FENCE went AROUND. Tomorrow the FIELD fills IN.' Make the perimeter↔area contrast across days an explicit teacher line.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough.recovery_moves=['Trace edge with finger.', 'Drill around the edge.', 'Compare with area definition.'] — concrete but flat; no diagnostic-driven branching, and no named research grounding the perimeter-vs-area confusion as a documented G3 misconception.
category_feedback.required_fix: Cite Lehrer (2003) or Battista's spatial-reasoning work on length-vs-area confusion, then branch recovery_moves: if the child counts inside squares, route to edge-tracing + 'fence-walk' kinesthetic; if the child counts SIDES (not lengths), route to ruler measurement of one side and additive sum. Two diagnostic-conditioned branches, named in the walkthrough.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: consolidation.exit_routine='Each child shares ONE: I measured ___ with perimeter ___ cm.' — a fill-in frame, not a memorable chant; Roo's 'Roo says — pick the right unit!' appears multiple times but is not a distinctive quotable refrain children would carry between lessons.
category_feedback.required_fix: Give Roo a short signature chant tied to perimeter that the class echoes at consolidation and that returns in Lessons 2-5 — e.g., 'AROUND, AROUND, add it all UP! That's perimeter — fill the cup!' or 'Hop the edge, hop the edge, ADD them up — Roo's perimeter pledge!' Drop it into minds_on once and consolidation as the closer; children chant back.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: action.steps[4]='Help with addition strategy — column or in-pairs. Show: add pairs first.' — teacher hands the strategy to children; no invitation for children to invent or compare addition strategies for summing 3-4 sides, and no research-grounded naming of the misconception (perimeter-as-area or count-of-sides rather than sum-of-lengths).
category_feedback.required_fix: Add an invent-and-compare moment to action: 'Pairs find perimeter of the hexagon (6 sides of 2 cm) ANY way. Share two ways.' Elicit at least 2: repeated addition, doubles, or 6x2. Name in expanded_walkthrough that this is Carpenter & Moser's count-all to count-on to known-fact progression.

summary: Pair 1 is solidly Achieving but does not clear the strict bar (4 categories at 3). Lesson is well-structured with optional puppet, realistic timing, faithful worksheet mapping, and a real perimeter-vs-area trap. To pass: add an explicit Lesson 2 bridge, cite research and branch recovery_moves on the perimeter-vs-area trap, give Roo a signature chant for the exit, and let children invent/compare addition strategies for summing sides.
